plan.hypothesis: H0: All group means are equal; H1: At least one group mean differs
assumptions: Independent observations within and between groups
Balanced design with equal group sizes
scientific_notes: Eta-squared (η²) is interpreted as proportion of variance in the outcome explained by group membership
Omnibus F-test is two-sided by convention for ANOVA
Effect size classification: η² = 0.06 is a small-to-medium effect (Cohen's benchmarks: 0.01 small, 0.06 medium, 0.14 large)
The non-centrality parameter λ = (η² / (1 - η²)) × (N / k) where N is total sample size and k is number of groups

answer.summary: A balanced one-way fixed-effects ANOVA with 3 independent normal groups and common variance, targeting 80% power for the omnibus F-test at α = 0.05 with population eta-squared = 0.06, requires a minimum of 52 participants per group (total N = 156). This design achieves an actual power of 0.8056, which exceeds the 80% target. The preceding admissible design (n = 51 per group) yields only 0.7973 power, falling below target.
answer.method: Analytic power inversion using pwr::pwr.anova.test (one-way ANOVA, balanced design). Eta-squared was converted to Cohen's f via f = √(η² / (1 − η²)) = 0.252646. The continuous solution of 51.3264 participants per group was rounded up to the minimum integer 52 per group that achieves ≥80% power.
assumptions: Homogeneity of variance across groups (common σ²)
Independent observations within and between groups
Balanced design with equal group sizes (n per group)
Fixed effects model (group effects are constants)
limitations: Power calculation assumes population parameters are exactly as specified; sensitivity to misspecification of η² is not examined
Calculation uses large-sample normal approximation to non-central F distribution (standard in pwr package)
No adjustment for multiple comparisons in post-hoc tests; result applies only to omnibus F-test
Balanced design assumption; unequal group sizes would require different calculation

executions.code:
library(pwr)

# Design parameters
k <- 3  # number of groups
eta_sq <- 0.06  # eta-squared effect size
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level
target_power <- 0.8  # target power
allocation_ratio <- 1  # balanced design

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# Relationship: f = sqrt(eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))
f_effect <- sqrt(eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))

cat("Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Number of groups (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Eta-squared (η²):", eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Converted to Cohen's f:", round(f_effect, 6), "\n")
cat("Alpha (significance level):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

# Use pwr::pwr.anova.test to find required n (per group)
# This function returns the per-group sample size for a balanced design
power_result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power
)

# Extract per-group sample size and round up to nearest integer
n_per_group_continuous <- power_result$n
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_per_group_continuous)

cat("Continuous solution (n per group):", round(n_per_group_continuous, 4), "\n")
cat("Minimum integer n per group:", n_per_group, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at selected design
power_at_selected <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  n = n_per_group,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha
)$power

cat("Achieved power at n =", n_per_group, "per group:", round(power_at_selected, 6), "\n")

# Verify power at the preceding integer design
n_preceding <- n_per_group - 1
if (n_preceding > 0) {
  power_at_preceding <- pwr.anova.test(
    k = k,
    n = n_preceding,
    f = f_effect,
    sig.level = alpha
  )$power
  
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_preceding, "per group):", round(power_at_preceding, 6), "\n")
}

# Summary table
cat("\n" + "="*60 + "\n")
cat("SUMMARY TABLE:\n")
cat("="*60 + "\n")
summary_table <- data.frame(
  "n_per_group" = c(n_preceding, n_per_group),
  "Total_N" = c(n_preceding * k, n_per_group * k),
  "Power" = c(round(power_at_preceding, 4), round(power_at_selected, 4)),
  "Meets_Target" = c(
    ifelse(power_at_preceding >= target_power, "Yes", "No"),
    ifelse(power_at_selected >= target_power, "Yes", "No")
  )
)

print(summary_table)

# Final result
cat("\n" + "="*60 + "\n")
cat("FINAL ANSWER:\n")
cat("="*60 + "\n")
cat("Minimum participants per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * k, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_at_selected, 6), "\n")

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
results_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_group, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = n_per_group * k, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_selected, 6), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "cohens_f_effect", value = round(f_effect, 6), unit = "effect_size")
  )
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(results_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Evidence e2; success=true

library(pwr)

# Design parameters
k <- 3  # number of groups
eta_sq <- 0.06  # eta-squared effect size
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level
target_power <- 0.8  # target power

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# Relationship: f = sqrt(eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))
f_effect <- sqrt(eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))

cat("Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Number of groups (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Eta-squared (η²):", eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Converted to Cohen's f:", round(f_effect, 6), "\n")
cat("Alpha (significance level):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

# Use pwr::pwr.anova.test to find required n (per group)
# This function returns the per-group sample size for a balanced design
power_result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power
)

# Extract per-group sample size and round up to nearest integer
n_per_group_continuous <- power_result$n
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_per_group_continuous)

cat("Continuous solution (n per group):", round(n_per_group_continuous, 4), "\n")
cat("Minimum integer n per group:", n_per_group, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at selected design
power_at_selected <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  n = n_per_group,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha
)$power

cat("Achieved power at n =", n_per_group, "per group:", round(power_at_selected, 6), "\n")

# Verify power at the preceding integer design
n_preceding <- n_per_group - 1
if (n_preceding > 0) {
  power_at_preceding <- pwr.anova.test(
    k = k,
    n = n_preceding,
    f = f_effect,
    sig.level = alpha
  )$power
  
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_preceding, "per group):", round(power_at_preceding, 6), "\n")
}

# Summary table
cat("\n", rep("=", 60), "\n", sep = "")
cat("SUMMARY TABLE:\n")
cat(rep("=", 60), "\n", sep = "")
summary_table <- data.frame(
  "n_per_group" = c(n_preceding, n_per_group),
  "Total_N" = c(n_preceding * k, n_per_group * k),
  "Power" = c(round(power_at_preceding, 4), round(power_at_selected, 4)),
  "Meets_Target" = c(
    ifelse(power_at_preceding >= target_power, "Yes", "No"),
    ifelse(power_at_selected >= target_power, "Yes", "No")
  )
)

print(summary_table)

# Final result
cat("\n", rep("=", 60), "\n", sep = "")
cat("FINAL ANSWER:\n")
cat(rep("=", 60), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Minimum participants per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * k, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_at_selected, 6), "\n")

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
results_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_group, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = n_per_group * k, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_selected, 6), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "cohens_f_effect", value = round(f_effect, 6), unit = "effect_size")
  )
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(results_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
